{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-23: *"should we ever just completely bring in dynograph-foundation into reflow2? we can cannibalize it and only take what we need/want and no longer have it as an external dependency?"*

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐ WHY THIS IS NOT THE QUESTION HE ALREADY SAID NO TO

`dec:idea-swap-dynograph-foundation-as-the-substitutability-demo` is **REJECTED** — his words, 2026-08-20: *"I don't want to really swap out dynograph-foundation (it works and putting a lot of effort into this is probably not worth it if we aren't going to really swap it out)."* The reason recorded there is general: **a demo that costs as much as the real thing is not a demo.**

THAT OBJECTION DOES NOT REACH THIS IDEA, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE POINT. Swapping means REIMPLEMENTING the functionality behind a contract. Cannibalising means KEEPING THE SAME CODE and moving it in-tree. The rejected option pays full replacement cost; this one pays relocation cost. They are answers to the same underlying question — what to do about the dynograph dependency — and only one of them was priced.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📐 THE MEASUREMENT THAT MATTERS HERE IS NOT THE ONE THE REJECTED NODE MADE

That node measured FILES IMPORTING each crate — 48 / 21 / 3 / 2 / 1 — and concluded that `dynograph_core` at 48 files "is not a module, it is the type vocabulary", so replacing it is a rewrite wearing substitution's name. **That is correct for REPLACEMENT and irrelevant to ABSORPTION**: blast radius measures how much would have to change if the types changed, and vendoring changes no types at all.

THE RELEVANT NUMBER IS THE IMPORTED SURFACE. Measured at HEAD 2026-08-23 from every `use dynograph_*` in `crates/` — **about 21 named items across five crates**:

  dynograph_core      DynoError · Value · Schema · PropertyDef · PropertyType ·
                      NodeTypeDef · EdgeTypeDef · EdgeEndpoint            (8)
  dynograph_storage   StoredNode · StoredEdge · StorageEngine · Value      (4)
  dynograph_graph     GraphBuilder · leiden · strongly_connected_components ·
                      connected_components · find_cycle · cut_structure    (6)
  dynograph_resolution  token_sort_ratio                                   (1)
  dynograph_vector      mean · linear_regression_slope                     (2)

⚠️ BOUND, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: this counts what is NAMED at an import site. It is a measure of the API SURFACE CONSUMED, not of the code volume behind it — `StorageEngine` is one name in front of a RocksDB-backed store, and `leiden` is one name in front of a community-detection implementation. It is a lower bound on work and an upper bound on interface.

⭐ TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE REJECTED NODE'S STATED RISKS, found by looking at what is actually imported rather than at which files import it:

· It warned *"vector search and HNSW are not trivial to reimplement well"*. **reflow2 does not use HNSW, or vector search, at all.** It imports `mean` and `linear_regression_slope` — arithmetic, in one file (`dimensions.rs`). Whatever the case against absorbing `dynograph_vector`, it is not that one.
· `dynograph_resolution` is one function, `token_sort_ratio` — fuzzy string matching, two import sites.

AND ONE RISK IT DID NOT NAME: `dynograph_graph` is where the real intellectual content sits — **leiden community detection, SCC, cycle finding, connected components, cut structure**. Six names, and the ones you would least want to reimplement. Under ABSORPTION that inverts into an argument FOR: you keep the implementation, so difficulty-to-rewrite stops being a cost and becomes the reason the code is worth having in-tree.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ THE OBVIOUS RISK THAT IS ALREADY ANSWERED

"Does this break storyflow, which also depends on dynograph?" — No. `fact:the-diamond-meets-at-dynographs-internals-not-its-interface` measured it: storyflow consumes dynograph as a **REST API over HTTP**; reflow2 consumes it as a **Rust library API**. Disjoint surfaces over one shared implementation. reflow2 dropping the Rust surface cannot touch storyflow's endpoints.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
IDEAS, UNRANKED, each with what it costs

**A. ABSORB EVERYTHING — vendor all five crates in, delete what is unimported, drop the git dependency.** What the question literally asks. Ends the upgrade treadmill, the tag pins, and the `[patch]` dance in `Cargo.toml`; makes reflow2 a single tree with no external source.
   ⚠️ You inherit maintenance of a RocksDB storage engine and a Leiden implementation forever, and you lose the upstream's fixes silently rather than by a pin bump you can read. **Vendoring converts a visible dependency into an invisible one** — the version pin at `reflow2.toml:11` currently carries a written reason for every bump, and that record has no successor once the code is in-tree.

**B. ABSORB THE THREE SMALL ONES ONLY — graph, resolution, vector (9 of the 21 items) — and keep core+storage as the external dependency.** The three that are algorithms rather than substrate.
   ⚠️ Honest counter, and it is the same one the rejected node made about its option C: **the dependency stays, so the treadmill stays.** The saving is partial and must not be sold as removal. What it does buy is that the two crates you would most struggle to justify rewriting are the ones you stop being able to lose.

**C. ABSORB ONLY WHAT IS TINY AND OWNED-BY-ACCIDENT — `token_sort_ratio` (1), `mean` and `linear_regression_slope` (2).** Three functions, almost certainly a few dozen lines, that reflow2 could own outright with no maintenance story worth the name.
   ⭐ Highest ratio of dependency-surface-removed to risk-taken. Removes two entire crates from the manifest.
   ⚠️ And it is nearly cosmetic: `dynograph-core` and `dynograph-storage` are what the dependency actually IS. Two fewer lines in `Cargo.toml` is not independence.

**D. DO NOTHING — it works, it is maintained, and the pin has a reason written on every bump.** The status quo, and what his own standing anti-over-engineering position argues for by default.
   ⚠️ The counter: the reason for absorbing is not technical, it is about what reflow2 IS. A design brain whose substrate is somebody else's repository has a supply chain; one that owns its tree does not. Whether that matters is a judgement about the product, not about the code.

**E. SETTLE THE PRIOR QUESTION FIRST — `dec:idea-is-the-foundation-a-subsystem-or-a-supplier`, still open.** Is dynograph a NINTH SUBSYSTEM of reflow2, or a supplier reached across required interfaces?
   ⭐ **This idea would answer that question by construction rather than by argument.** Absorb it and it is a subsystem; there is no supplier left to be. That may be the strongest thing in favour of A — it dissolves an open modelling question instead of settling it on paper — and equally the strongest reason to answer the prior question first, since doing it in this order decides by doing.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📌 WHAT NOBODY HAS COSTED, so the list is not read as an estimate

No measurement exists of the LINE COUNT behind those 21 names, of what the five crates carry that reflow2 never touches, or of how much of `dynograph-storage` is RocksDB glue versus reflow2-specific. "21 imported items" is an interface measurement and says nothing about how big the tree is that would move. **The cheap next step, if any of this is pursued, is to measure the code volume behind each crate and how much of it is dead from reflow2's point of view** — which is exactly the "only take what we need/want" half of his question, and the half that currently has no number attached to it at all.","name":"OPEN — should reflow2 absorb dynograph-foundation outright, keeping only the ~21 items it actually imports, and stop having an external dependency at all?","rationale":"Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`. Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-23, immediately after the v0.39.0 cut. Nothing here is intent and nothing is planned.

DEDUP: the guard surfaced `dec:idea-swap-dynograph-foundation-as-the-substitutability-demo` and `dec:idea-is-the-foundation-a-subsystem-or-a-supplier`; both were read in full and judged DIFFERENT. The first is REJECTED and asks about REPLACING the foundation with a new implementation — a cost this idea does not incur, because absorbing keeps the code. The second asks what the foundation IS; this asks what to DO with it, and would answer that one by construction rather than by argument.","status":"proposed"}
